long_biography.plain_text:
Slim trained as a civil engineer and taught algebra while studying in Mexico City. He formed a brokerage and property company in 1965, then built Grupo Carso by buying underpriced businesses during periods of economic stress. The pivotal expansion arrived when a Carso-led consortium acquired Telmex in 1990 and developed its mobile operations into América Móvil.

He has transferred day-to-day leadership of much of the group to the next generation while remaining honorary chairman of América Móvil, Telmex, Grupo Carso and Inbursa. His family retains control through direct holdings, a family trust and investment vehicles, while he still chairs selected infrastructure and philanthropic organisations. Telecommunications remains the central business within his investment interests, complemented by finance, retail, construction, mining and property holdings. Shareholdings underpin his fortune; corporate revenue, network assets, market capitalisation and foundation endowments belong to the respective companies or charities.
